clue.text: Had spell on base, with long leave finally included

indicators.note: included says the run of pieces sits inside the base word

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a flower bed or the bed of a road
to itch for something is to long for it

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word leave

explanation.surface: A soldier on base is caught by a spell while his long leave runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military base in the surface, but it means a bed. 'finally' takes only the closing E of 'leave', and 'included' sets the pieces inside, between the E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to cast a spell on someone, so the past participle matches the phrase about having been enchanted.

clue.text: Plant ready for security fences in seconds

indicators.note: fences in means the bail word encloses the other

parts.note: ready money put up as security is bail

explanation.surface: A plant is ready to be secured behind fences in seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash, so cash put down as security is BAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary herb, a plant of the mint family.

clue.text: How insult might be returned or handled

explanation.walkthrough: 'With knobs on' is British slang for returning something even more emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means repaid with interest, as an insult thrown back harder; the other means having handles.

clue.text: Some canvas shirts are poorly put together

parts.note: shirts are tops
to ail is to be poorly or ill

explanation.surface: Some canvas shirts are badly assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' means sails, not fabric for shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest on a mast, and sails are canvas.

clue.text: Prostitution gets group into bother

indicators.note: into puts the group inside the bother word

parts.note: to harry is to bother or harass
a lot is a group, as in that lot

explanation.surface: Prostitution lands a group in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlotry is the practice of a harlot, an old word for prostitute.

clue.text: Nodding agreement, having no English word for recall

indicators.note: recall reads as call back, so the whole run turns backwards
having no takes the English letter out of the agreement

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Someone nods in agreement, lacking the English word to recall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes E from YES, leaving YS; 'recall' reverses YSWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy person is nodding off, about to fall asleep.

clue.text: Goddess with every second going far —- very far

indicators.note: dropping every second letter keeps the odd letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A goddess travels far, very far, as every second passes.
explanation.walkthrough: From FARVERYFAR, losing every second letter leaves the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility, a familiar crossword deity.

clue.text: Partner no longer in cast getting tense

indicators.note: in places the former partner within the throwing word

parts.note: to fling is to cast or throw
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex-partner in the theatre cast becomes nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' is a verb, not actors; 'tense' means tightening muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexing a muscle makes it tighten, so flexing is making something tense.

clue.text: Old prior to deputise for prelate, taking tips

indicators.note: tips here are the final letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An old deputy stands in for a bishop and takes the gratuities.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is the archaic word for before, so old prior to is the poetic sense.

clue.text: Player out with fracture prepared comeback

indicators.note: a fracture breaks the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A player is sidelined with a broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fracture' rearranges PLAYER OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic reply is a response readied in advance, sent back without thought.

clue.text: It takes physical effort not to crash

explanation.surface: Staying upright demands effort if one is not to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' is slang for going to sleep, so staying up late means not crashing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the stomach exercise done lying down; the other is staying awake past bedtime.

clue.text: Teddy's little jumper elegant with its tail tucked in

definitions.note: read as Teddy is, so the definition is the nickname Teddy

parts.note: a roo is a young or small kangaroo, a jumping animal

indicators.note: the final letter is moved from the end into the middle of the word

parts.note: svelte means slim and elegant

explanation.surface: Someone's teddy bear wears a small, smart jumper with its hem tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with its tail tucked in' shifts the final E of the elegant word inward. 'Teddy's' reads as 'Teddy is'; the teddy bear was named after this president.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt, the US president, was nicknamed Teddy, and gave his name to the teddy bear.

clue.text: So very smart of a pet to tuck into fancy meal

indicators.note: the pet phrase goes inside the pair of words, between them

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
dinner is a meal
of a pet means belonging to a dog, a pet's possessive

explanation.surface: A pet digs into an elaborate meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tuck into' looks like eating, but it places the pet phrase between the other two words. The idiom means dressed up showily, so the definition is mildly ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed up like a dog's dinner is a British idiom for very smart, often flashily so.

clue.text: Close down repeatedly

explanation.walkthrough: To neck a drink is British slang for downing it quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is level in a race; the other is to neck, or gulp down, drink again and again.

clue.text: Stalkers disastrous for East End's public image?

parts.note: PR, public relations, manages public image

indicators.note: a Cockney in London's East End drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: howlers are disastrous blunders

explanation.surface: Stalkers would be a disaster for the image of London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home to Cockney speech, which drops initial H, so HOWLERS becomes OWLERS. PR howlers are blunders bad for public image.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowlers creep about looking for prey or victims, just as stalkers do.

clue.text: Dealt with murder suspect, and went swiftly to bed?

indicators.note: with says the suspect goes alongside the dealing word

parts.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in the board game Cluedo
meted means dealt out

explanation.surface: Having dealt with a murder suspect, the detective hurried off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo, called Clue in the US, is a murder mystery board game. 'bed' means the sea bed, not sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, as a stone dropping fast to the sea bed.

clue.text: Breakfast placed here for one rising after gong

indicators.note: after puts the rising piece behind the medal

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one
gong is slang for a medal, and the GC is the George Cross
up means rising

explanation.surface: A breakfast gong sounds and someone gets up for their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Cross is a British gallantry medal; 'gong' is British slang for any medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg, the breakfast item, is set in this small holder at the table.

clue.text: Strip end off cutlet, sticking quietly in soup

indicators.note: in puts the quiet letter inside the strip

parts.note: the Gaza Strip, shortened to Gaza
P is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: end off means the final letter is cut away

parts.note: a chop is a cutlet of meat

explanation.surface: A cook trims a cutlet and quietly drops it into soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end off' removes the final P of CHOP. 'Strip' means the Gaza Strip, not stripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazpacho is a cold Spanish soup of tomato and vegetables.

clue.text: Relief as nudist returned clothes giving no protection

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
clothes means the words wrap around the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A naturist enjoys the relief of wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'clothes' into the definition; it is the indicator, the words clothing the run. 'returned' reads EFASNU backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offering no protection leaves one exposed to danger, the opposite of secure.

clue.text: Put on record with fine beat

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
logged means put on record

explanation.surface: A fine beat is put on record.
explanation.definitionFit: Flogged means beaten with a whip, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Like old soldier, perhaps, on guard outside exhibit

indicators.note: outside says the cautious word goes round the other

parts.note: wary means on guard
to wear clothes or an expression is to exhibit them

explanation.surface: An old soldier stands guard outside an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran may well be tired of fighting after long service, and the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Rather frail partners holding hands getting a peck from a drunk

parts.note: West and East are partners at bridge, holding hands of cards
a drunk slurs the word kiss, a peck, as kish

explanation.surface: Couples holding hands get a kiss from a tipsy stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, W and E play as partners; 'hands' are their cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means rather, so weakish is rather weak or frail.

clue.text: Lessons for fitness fanatic eating a sort of butter

indicators.note: eating says the pair takes in the other letter

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school lessons for fitness
a nut is a fanatic, as in health nut

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic in a lesson is eating a spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a spread, so peanut names a type of butter.

clue.text: To avoid offence, head person's getting weakest and strongest on board

parts.note: to head something can mean to mind it, as a supervisor
one's is the possessive of the indefinite person
pawns, P in chess notation, are the weakest pieces
queens, Q in chess notation, are the strongest pieces

explanation.surface: A tactful head teacher takes care of the weak and strong on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' points to the chessboard, where pawns are weakest and the queen strongest.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding your manners, being careful about speech and behaviour, is how one avoids offending people.

clue.text: Sibling hugging Nancy's the uncle of Le Fanu

indicators.note: hugging means the sibling wraps around the French word

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling
in Nancy, a French city, the word for the is la

explanation.surface: A sister embraces Nancy, whose uncle was the writer Le Fanu.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is a city in France, not a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Silas is the title character of the 1864 novel by Sheridan Le Fanu.

clue.text: Nice to watch niece get excited, clutching pound

indicators.note: clutching says the shuffled letters hold the pound sign
excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A niece gets thrilled watching, grabbing a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city or a pleasant adjective; it belongs to the definition. 'excited' rearranges the eight letters to TEEGENIC, and 'clutching' puts the pound sign inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone telegenic looks good on television, making them pleasant to watch.

clue.text: In E. Europe, change oil perhaps after failing to start up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
failing to start takes away the first letter

parts.note: oil is an example of fuel

explanation.surface: In Eastern Europe someone changes the oil after the car fails to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' drops F, leaving UEL, which 'up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The leu is the currency of Romania and Moldova, money being change.

clue.text: Confession from one putting hands round model

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, and also the speaker
to deal is to give out hands of cards around the table

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to wandering hands around a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confession from one putting hands round' is the card dealer's own words, 'I deal'; the surface hints at groping.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or standard, as a model is.

clue.text: Finished without tackling game old priest

indicators.note: tackling suggests gripping, so the first word holds the game

parts.note: did means finished, as in did the job
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Having done with a match, without tackling anyone, an old priest retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is an old link meaning outside, reinforcing the container. RU, rugby union, is a common crossword game.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids were priests of the ancient Celts, so an old priest suits them.

clue.text: A second filming session's needed to capture unusual show

indicators.note: to capture means the filming word surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: a take is a filming session, here plural

indicators.note: unusual means the letters come in an odd order

explanation.surface: A second session of filming is needed to get a strange performance on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A second' looks like a second take, but it is the definition. 'unusual' rearranges the four letters to WOSH, which 'to capture' places inside the filming word.
explanation.definitionFit: In two shakes is an idiom for very quickly, so the phrase means a moment or second.
